title: Chicken Passanda
subtitle: Mild almond and cream curry
excerpt: Chicken thighs simmered in a mild, creamy almond sauce. Passanda is one of the mildest curry-house dishes, with a silky texture and a gentle warmth that makes it good for those who prefer less heat.

recipe.sourceNotes: Passanda originates in the Mughal court cuisine of North India, where it referred to a technique of flattening and marinating meat. In the UK curry-house tradition it evolved into a mild, cream-and-almond dish, distinct from the original and broadly popular with those who avoid heat.

recipeTools.notes: For the sauce and simmering the chicken.

content.text: Chicken passanda is a mild curry built on a base of onion, garlic, and warm spices finished with ground almonds and double cream. The result is a rich, silky sauce with no significant heat. It works well for a crowd where tolerance for chilli varies, and leftovers reheat well the next day when the flavours have deepened.

items.preparation: boneless, skinless, cut into 4 cm pieces

content.text: Coat the chicken pieces in the yoghurt and leave to marinate for at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or overnight in the fridge.
Heat the oil in a large pan over medium heat. Add the cardamom pods and cinnamon stick and fry for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the onions and cook for 12 to 15 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes. Add the garam masala, ground coriander, and turmeric, stir for 1 minute.
Add the marinated chicken and stir to coat in the spice base. Cook for 5 minutes over medium-high heat until the chicken starts to colour.
Stir in the ground almonds, then add 200 ml water and the salt. Bring to a simmer and cook on low heat for 20 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Stir in the double cream and heat through for 2 minutes without boiling. Remove the cardamom and cinnamon. Scatter over the toasted flaked almonds and serve with rice or naan.
